label: prf:adelic-reeb-restricted-product
title: Proof of adelic reeb restricted product
html:
Both parts are proved over the abstract value group \Gamma. The restricted-product condition is encoded by an explicit finite set S of active places (those with \ordw_v \neq 0); off S the local order is the tame archimedean reference 0, so the sum is finite and well-defined. Additivity is pointwise addition of local orders summed over S (\sum_S (a+b) = \sum_S a + \sum_S b). The squeeze is the strict comparison of finite sums: a finite sum of weak inequalities with one strict term is strict. \square

Tate's thesis. This is the surreal-register form of Tate's adelic factorisation [tate1967]: where Tate writes the global zeta integral as a restricted product of local zeta integrals \zeta_v(f_v, s) — one per place — the substrate writes the global Reeb infinitesimal \varepsilon as the restricted product of local \varepsilon_v, and the global valuation as the sum of local valuations. Part 1 is the valuation-theoretic shadow of the Euler product; part 2 gives a separate squeeze at each prime.

Extra structure — consistency across places. The hypothesis that all local orders \ordw_v land in one common value group \Gamma is not free: it is the requirement that the per-place surreal orders be commensurable — a single coherent birthday filtration spanning every prime and the archimedean place v = \infty simultaneously. Without it the sum \sum_v \ordw_v(f_v) does not even typecheck. This shared \Gamma is the genuine additional structure the adelic lift exposes (a linearly ordered abelian group).
